title: Totalization of a natural ordinary open tensor comparison
statement: Let (C,J,R) and (C′,J′,R′) be essentially coefficient-small ringed sites with independently sized object and morphism universes, with the canonical ordinary tensor, total tensor and summand insertions of [def-coef-semilinear-system-models]. Let F from open to ambient modules and G in the other direction be additive functors with F left adjoint to G. Given isomorphisms (F M) tensor N isomorphic to F(M tensor G N), natural simultaneously in M and N, there are isomorphisms totalTensor(F P,Q) isomorphic to F(totalTensor(P,G Q)) for all unbounded cochain complexes P,Q. Their degree-k components compose with each (a,b)-summand insertion, a+b=k, as the given ordinary comparison followed by F of the open insertion. They are natural simultaneously in both complexes. No restriction tensorator or flatness hypothesis is required.

source.place: Tag 0GL1, total tensor comparison; Homology Tag 012Z for direct-sum totalization.

proof.text: Supply the canonical independently sized monoidal and total-bifunctor instances. The left adjoint F preserves the small coproducts in each total degree. Invert the given ordinary comparison and its naturality square, and apply comparisonFromComponents_exists from RingedOpenTotalTensorKFlat, with its canonical total presentations. This produces F(total(P,GQ)) isomorphic to total(FP,Q), its insertion formula and simultaneous naturality. The construction commutes with each differential by the ordinary naturality squares, including the signed second differential.

Invert this cochain isomorphism. In each degree, postcompose the required insertion identity with the invertible forward comparison; its known insertion formula and the ordinary inverse identities give equality. Apply the inverse-square identity to the known cochain naturality to obtain the simultaneous naturality of the inverse comparison. These operations require no boundedness or flatness.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0GL1 and Homology 012Z; reuse of the fully proved generic component totalization and inversion of its identities.

theorem nativeOpenTensor_totalization_exists
    {C : Type c} [Category.{v} C] [EssentiallySmall.{max c v r} C]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{max c v r})
    {C' : Type c} [Category.{v} C'] [EssentiallySmall.{max c v r} C']
    (J' : GrothendieckTopology C') (R' : Sheaf J' CommRingCat.{max c v r})
    (F : SemilinearSections.Mod.{c, v, max c v r} J' R' ⥤
      SemilinearSections.Mod.{c, v, max c v r} J R)
    (G : SemilinearSections.Mod.{c, v, max c v r} J R ⥤
      SemilinearSections.Mod.{c, v, max c v r} J' R')
    [hF : F.Additive] [hG : G.Additive] (adj : F ⊣ G)
    (ordinary : ∀ (M : SemilinearSections.Mod.{c, v, max c v r} J' R')
      (N : SemilinearSections.Mod.{c, v, max c v r} J R),
      ordinaryTensor.{c, v, r} J R (F.obj M) N ≅
        F.obj (ordinaryTensor.{c, v, r} J' R' M (G.obj N)))
    (hn : ∀ {M M' : SemilinearSections.Mod.{c, v, max c v r} J' R'}
      {N N' : SemilinearSections.Mod.{c, v, max c v r} J R} (f : M ⟶ M') (g : N ⟶ N'),
      ordinaryTensorHom.{c, v, r} J R (F.map f) g ≫ (ordinary M' N').hom =
        (ordinary M N).hom ≫ F.map (ordinaryTensorHom.{c, v, r} J' R' f (G.map g))) :
    ∃ chain : ∀ (P : CochainComplex (SemilinearSections.Mod.{c, v, max c v r} J' R') ℤ)
        (Q : CochainComplex (SemilinearSections.Mod.{c, v, max c v r} J R) ℤ),
      (totalTensor.{c, v, r} J R).obj ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P, Q) ≅
        (F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj ((totalTensor.{c, v, r} J' R').obj
          (P, (G.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj Q)),
      (∀ P Q (a b k : ℤ) (h : a + b = k),
        tensorSummand.{c, v, r} J R ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P) Q a b k h ≫
            (chain P Q).hom.f k =
          (ordinary (P.X a) (Q.X b)).hom ≫
            F.map (tensorSummand.{c, v, r} J' R' P
              ((G.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj Q) a b k h)) ∧
      (∀ {P P' : CochainComplex (SemilinearSections.Mod.{c, v, max c v r} J' R') ℤ}
        {Q Q' : CochainComplex (SemilinearSections.Mod.{c, v, max c v r} J R) ℤ}
        (f : P ⟶ P') (g : Q ⟶ Q'),
        (totalTensor.{c, v, r} J R).map
            (Prod.mkHom ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).map f) g) ≫ (chain P' Q').hom =
          (chain P Q).hom ≫ (F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).map
            ((totalTensor.{c, v, r} J' R').map
              (Prod.mkHom f ((G.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).map g))))
